content: We need to determine number of carbonyl groups in the sample's compound. We have no direct description of the compound. We can use IR spectra to detect C=O stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons (~190-220 ppm). Also could use 13C NMR. Since we need count of carbonyl groups, best to get carbon NMR and count peaks in carbonyl region. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool. That will give list of chemical shifts. Then count those in typical carbonyl range (190-220 ppm). Let's do that.
